subject: Interpretation of spatial predictions of density

messages.author: b0084e74319ebcb3
messages.subject: Interpretation of spatial predictions of density
parts:
Hi all,

I did spatial predictions of density (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/vignettes/spp-dist.pdf) using unmarked but I am not sure on how to interpret the results. Do the predicted values correspond to actual density or should be interpreted as a relative measure? Just to be conservative I am interpreting this as relative not face values. I am interested in showing which geographic areas are predicted to have higher densities of the species according to environmental conditions (cloud cover, elevation and tree biomass), not in making any inferences about actual population size.

I appreciate any insights in this subject! Thank you all in advance.

Best,

Laura

messages.author: 0c8e4d9395a2aae5
messages.subject: Re: Interpretation of spatial predictions of density
parts:
Laura, if you believe your models have accounted for variation in detectability, then you should be able to interpret predicted values as density, if you have a defined survey area.  If you don't know the area you're surveying, then you can still make comparisons treating the predictions as relative measures, as you stated.  This assumes however that your survey plots, though of unknown area, are the same across samples, which can be questionable. 

Mike Worland

messages.author: b0084e74319ebcb3
messages.subject: Re: Interpretation of spatial predictions of density
parts:
Thank you very much Mike. I do not think that my models accounted for variation in detectability, therefore I prefer to treat them as relative measure. 
Best,
Laura
